primary_mechanism: weak hydrodynamic perturbation or group tide
hi_evidence: The H I disk extends slightly beyond the optical disk and is broadly symmetric but warped; the southeastern side has locally enhanced H I.
multiwavelength_evidence: Halpha and radio emission are also enhanced to the southeast. VIVA notes its likely M-cloud/background location and nearby dwarf companions, so neither ICM compression nor a tidal origin is uniquely selected.
event_sequence: A largely gas-normal disk was mildly disturbed; no evidence establishes a completed stripping passage.
timing: No published pericentric or quenching clock was found; only a present-day weak-disturbance state is defensible.
contradictions: Yoon class 0 and the absence of a Köppen entry agree that a strong stripping history is unproven, but do not distinguish tide, warp, or weak ram pressure.
gfmr_implication: Any metallicity-SFR offset should be interpreted as a possible local gas-supply or compression effect, not as a calibrated infall-time sequence.
mauve_tests: Use MUSE gas-star kinematic residuals and outer-disk abundance asymmetry; compare the southeastern sector to the opposite side and to resolved CO.

hi_evidence: M98 has an extended, asymmetric southeastern H I distribution and a warp but is not strongly H I deficient in the adopted catalogue context.
multiwavelength_evidence: The central gas field is bar-distorted. MAUVE-MUSE finds resolved ionized-gas/metallicity structure, but these data do not by themselves prove a stripping epoch.
event_sequence: An intrinsically warped barred disk may be experiencing low-level pressure; a severe completed event is not required by its current gas reservoir.
timing: No tailored clock. Köppen labels a low-deficiency active case, whereas Yoon class IV is morphology-based and MAUVE adopts pre-peak.
contradictions: This is a formal reclassification audit: Yoon IV would normally map to a slow/post category, while Köppen places it among low-deficiency active strippers. The retained pre-peak label records the lack of strong present truncation, not certainty about first infall.
history_confidence: moderate for weak processing; low for orbital stage
gfmr_implication: Because H I remains abundant, gas mass may still track inflow-like dilution more closely than SFR; bar-driven SFE changes and environmental gas removal are confounded.
mauve_tests: Measure leading/trailing metallicity and DIG asymmetries; combine MUSE with H I/CO velocity residuals before assigning a direction of motion.

primary_mechanism: none established; possible weak ram pressure
hi_evidence: The extended, non-deficient H I disk is warped but lacks the bridge or one-sided truncation expected for a strong interaction with nearby NGC 4216.
multiwavelength_evidence: The stellar disk is comparatively regular. Survey radio/X-ray coverage supplies measurements but no dedicated causal history.
event_sequence: The galaxy is best treated as a minimally processed/weakly perturbed comparison object, with a possible early pressure signature left open.
timing: No dedicated timing constraint.
contradictions: Yoon class 0 conflicts mildly with Köppen's low-deficiency active assignment; both are low-leverage classifications for this object.
gfmr_implication: A near-normal gas reservoir makes this a useful control for separating ordinary resolved MZR/SFR structure from removal-driven offsets.
mauve_tests: Search for faint one-sided ionized gas and compare outer-disk CO/H I truncation radii; do not use phase space alone as an orbit.

hi_evidence: M99 has a strongly asymmetric disk and an approximately 250 kpc star-poor H I stream. The main disk remains H I rich rather than classically truncated.
multiwavelength_evidence: ALFALFA and numerical work connect the stream to a rapid fly-by; low-frequency radio asymmetry and VESTIGE Halpha knots in stripped gas indicate that ICM interaction may operate simultaneously.
event_sequence: A fast gravitational encounter generated the one-armed response and long tidal debris; subsequent/ongoing weak ram pressure modified diffuse gas and radio plasma without producing severe global deficiency.
timing: Tail models disagree in detail: a combined encounter model gives about 280 Myr since closest passage, whereas the VIRGOHI21 high-speed-tail model gives about 750 Myr. The difference is model-dependent, not a measurement error bar.
contradictions: Pure RPS cannot readily explain the star-poor 250 kpc feature, while pure tide underpredicts some radio/edge signatures. The weight of evidence favours a compound history; the identity of the perturber remains uncertain.
history_confidence: high for a past fast encounter; moderate for current RPS
gfmr_implication: Tidal gas rearrangement and weak stripping can change gas mass, SFE, and local dilution in different directions. A single pre-peak code is therefore insufficient for FMR interpretation.
mauve_tests: Map abundance and SFE along the one-arm/tail-launch geometry; test whether compressed radio edges correspond to enhanced CO or merely aged cosmic rays.

hi_evidence: A roughly 27 kpc gas-only H I tail and lopsided disk identify recent removal of diffuse gas.
multiwavelength_evidence: Nearby NGC 4299 and the disturbed stellar/gas geometry leave a tidal contribution plausible; large-scale radio work is consistent with an environmentally perturbed magnetized ISM.
event_sequence: A mild gravitational perturbation may have loosened outer gas, followed by or concurrent with an ICM wind that formed the one-sided tail.
timing: No tailored clock; the tail is a present/recent indicator rather than a quantified time to peak.
contradictions: Yoon I and Köppen active agree on ongoing/early processing but cannot apportion tide and RPS.
gfmr_implication: Gas loss can reduce H I before SFR responds, moving the galaxy off an H I-based gFMR while leaving the SFR-FMR temporarily less affected.
mauve_tests: Compare tail-side Halpha/metallicity to the leading half; model the NGC4294/4299 relative orbit before attributing all asymmetry to pressure.

hi_evidence: M100 is H I rich with a southwestern extension/warp and a faint bridge toward NGC 4323; there is no severe truncation.
multiwavelength_evidence: Rich CO and star-formation data mostly diagnose internal bar/spiral physics. Environmental survey studies supply context but no dedicated stripping history.
event_sequence: A mild companion interaction and/or weak ICM contact perturbed outer atomic gas while leaving the molecular/star-forming disk broadly normal.
timing: No event clock was found.
contradictions: Yoon 0 classifies no definite stripping, whereas Köppen's analytical selection lists it as low-deficiency active; the observations carry more weight than the analytical tag.
gfmr_implication: Internal bar/spiral SFE variations dominate many resolved relations; environmental interpretations require an outer-disk signature that is not yet isolated.
mauve_tests: Use MAUVE to separate bar/arm/interarm metallicity structure from the southwest H I anomaly and possible companion bridge.

hi_evidence: A sharp H I cutoff and short one-sided tail, together with a compressed edge, indicate current pressure.
multiwavelength_evidence: Radio compression supports an ICM wind; shell-like/offset stellar structure means gravity may also have disturbed the disk.
event_sequence: A galaxy on a high-velocity radial approach is losing its outer atomic gas now; a prior gravitational perturbation may explain the stellar asymmetry.
timing: No tailored numerical time; the morphology constrains an active stage only.
contradictions: Yoon I indicates early stripping, while Köppen assigns a past-strip solution. The disagreement shows how analytical deficiency fits can conflict with direct present morphology.
history_confidence: moderate-high for active RPS; low for prior tide
gfmr_implication: A leading-edge compression episode can transiently raise local SFR/SFE while global H I falls, so local and global FMR residuals need not share a sign.
mauve_tests: Test shocked/DIG gas at the compressed edge and derive stellar-versus-gas kinematic asymmetry to isolate a gravitational component.

primary_mechanism: recent gas acquisition and starburst feedback
hi_evidence: The H I disk is exceptionally massive and extended, with irregular outer clouds rather than a stripped/truncated morphology.
multiwavelength_evidence: MAUVE-MUSE resolves a roughly 6 kpc bipolar ionized outflow. The galaxy is a metallicity outlier below the ensemble rMZR; this is consistent with recent gas-supply disturbance but does not identify the donor or orbit.
event_sequence: External gas acquisition or a tidal perturbation plausibly fuelled a central starburst, which launched the observed wind; direct Virgo ICM stripping is not the dominant observed process.
timing: Outflow dynamical times are Myr-scale and source-dependent; no secure cluster-pericentre time exists. Do not equate the wind age with the interaction age.
contradictions: Yoon 0 and Köppen non-deficient agree against strong stripping. The accretion trigger is an inference from H I richness, morphology and metallicity, not a directly identified encounter.
history_confidence: high for feedback outflow; moderate for recent gas supply; low for orbital history
gfmr_implication: This is the clearest case where gas accretion/dilution and non-disk ionized emission can drive a gFMR/FMR residual independently of cluster stage; Halpha may not be a clean in-situ SFR proxy in the wind.
mauve_tests: Use CO/H I metallicity mixing maps, separate disk HII regions from outflow spaxels, and search deep imaging/kinematics for an accretion donor.

hi_evidence: A long northwestern H I tail and gas-free outer stellar disk favour removal of diffuse gas.
multiwavelength_evidence: The radio continuum does not show every expected wind diagnostic, so the tail geometry is not uniquely hydrodynamic; MAUVE ionized-gas data provide a current disk-state measurement.
event_sequence: Recent outer-disk gas loss is likely; a fast encounter may have contributed, but no perturber is securely tied to the event.
timing: No tailored timing constraint.
contradictions: Yoon I and Köppen active support ongoing processing, while the incomplete radio signature lowers mechanism confidence.
gfmr_implication: Outer gas removal should first change gas fraction and resolved radial sampling; an integrated metallicity increase could reflect loss of low-metallicity outskirts rather than rapid enrichment.
mauve_tests: Measure tail-side gas excitation and metallicity, and compare gas/stellar residual fields for a tidal impulse.

hi_evidence: The H I disk is extended and close to normal but has a cutoff on the M87-facing side and an extension on the opposite side.
multiwavelength_evidence: Radio asymmetry offers weak support for pressure; abundant PHANGS/VERTICO measurements otherwise emphasize internal disk dynamics.
event_sequence: A low-level ICM wind is beginning to reshape outer atomic gas without wholesale depletion.
timing: No tailored clock.
contradictions: Yoon I and Köppen active are consistent, but both evidence and effect size are modest.
gfmr_implication: This system tests the earliest regime where gas geometry changes before large SFR or metallicity offsets emerge.
mauve_tests: Target leading/trailing HII-region abundances and DIG, and compare CO/H I edge radii at matched sensitivity.

hi_evidence: H I connects the pair; assigning integrated H I flux to either component is uncertain in the overlap.
multiwavelength_evidence: CO and H I show enhanced molecular fraction in the overlap. ALMA resolves a continuous roughly 50 km/s connection and a 1.8 x 0.35 kpc molecular collision-front filament, but later line ratios indicate low excitation rather than a mature dense starburst ridge.
event_sequence: NGC4567 and NGC4568 are undergoing first close contact; localized gas compression and phase conversion precede any merger remnant or global starburst.
timing: The encounter is early/pre-coalescence, but no defensible absolute pericentre time or Virgo orbital clock is published; cloud free-fall times are not encounter ages.
contradictions: The system is Yoon 0 and absent from Köppen. Integrated SFR/SFE remains normal within scatter, so a collision front is not equivalent to global enhancement; cluster RPS is not securely established.
history_confidence: high for pair interaction; no secure pair or cluster clock
gfmr_implication: Localized H I-to-H2 conversion and mixing can affect resolved gFMR projections, but there is no direct abundance-dilution measurement and no demonstrated galaxy-wide SFE enhancement.
mauve_tests: Decompose MUSE velocities and metallicities by component and overlap; keep NGC4567 and NGC4568 gas budgets separate wherever the data allow.

secondary_mechanism: tidal compression/shear; no strong ICM stripping established
hi_evidence: H I bridges the pair, but component fluxes are blended; NGC4568 has its own catalogued gas and stellar properties.
multiwavelength_evidence: The molecular collision front is gravitationally bound but low excitation (maximum CO(3-2)/CO(1-0) about 0.17+/-0.04). Radio polarization is consistent with tidal compression/shear rather than strong ongoing RPS.
event_sequence: NGC4568 participates in the same first-contact event, with localized phase conversion/compression rather than evidence for global stripping or a mature overlap starburst.
timing: The encounter is early/pre-coalescence; no secure absolute encounter time or Virgo pericentre time is published.
contradictions: Yoon 0 and no Köppen entry support leaving the ICM history unclassified. Resolved SFE is at most slightly enhanced in the overlap and the pair-wide value is normal within uncertainty.
history_confidence: high for pair interaction; no secure pair or cluster clock
gfmr_implication: Local compression/mixing can move spaxels across resolved FMR projections without implying an ICM sequence; direct oxygen-abundance evidence is still needed.
mauve_tests: Fit two stellar/gas velocity systems and exclude overlap spaxels when establishing each component's baseline resolved MZR and SFE.

primary_mechanism: ram pressure plus interaction with NGC4302
hi_evidence: The H I disk is sharply cut on one side and diffuse on the other, with a disturbed distribution in the physical pair.
multiwavelength_evidence: A compressed radio edge supports an ICM wind; pair geometry and shared disturbances require a tidal contribution.
event_sequence: Mutual gravity perturbed the disks while ram pressure acted on exposed diffuse gas; neither mechanism alone explains every asymmetry.
timing: No tailored event time. The pair's current proximity is observed; a pericentric clock is not.
contradictions: Yoon II and Köppen active agree on current processing but cannot separate pair and cluster forces.
history_confidence: high for mixed processing; moderate for chronology
gfmr_implication: Gas redistribution/compression may raise local SFE even as H I is removed, creating different trajectories in gas-FMR and SFR-FMR space.
mauve_tests: Jointly model both disks with MUSE stellar/gas velocities, radio leading edges and CO compression; avoid treating pair membership as mere noise.

secondary_mechanism: interaction with NGC4298 and disk-halo flows
hi_evidence: The edge-on disk has a southern truncation and northern H I extension/tail.
multiwavelength_evidence: Diffuse ionized-gas halo and extraplanar material are well measured; radio data support environmental perturbation, while the companion can affect disk structure.
event_sequence: The ICM is displacing outer gas, superposed on an interacting edge-on pair and ordinary fountain/accretion flows.
timing: No robust stripping clock; morphology indicates a current/recent event.
contradictions: Yoon II and Köppen active converge on ongoing processing. Extraplanar gas is not automatically stripped gas because disk-halo circulation is an alternative.
gfmr_implication: Separating fountain gas from stripped gas is essential: recycled metal-rich extraplanar gas and externally removed low-density gas have opposite metallicity implications.
mauve_tests: Use line ratios, rotation lag and metallicity of extraplanar gas to distinguish fountain, accretion and ICM displacement.

hi_evidence: A sharply truncated H I disk and one-sided tail, with undisturbed outer stars, directly identify ongoing outside-in stripping.
multiwavelength_evidence: GALEX/VESTIGE show a radial quenching gradient; CO is also affected but less strongly. Ionized-gas kinematics trace stripped diffuse material.
event_sequence: Outer gas began disappearing first; the stripping front progressed inward while the galaxy approached peak pressure and continues to quench the disk outside-in.
timing: Tailored modelling places the galaxy about 100 Myr before peak. Resolved stellar-population fits find outer regions quenched roughly 400-600 Myr ago, the Halpha truncation radius about 100 Myr ago, and characteristic local SFR decay times near 50 Myr. These clocks measure different radii/processes.
contradictions: The model time to pressure peak is not the same as time since quenching at a given radius. Their apparent difference is physically expected in progressive outside-in stripping.
gfmr_implication: NGC4330 provides a time-ordered test: gas fraction falls first, local SFR follows quickly at each radius, and metallicity can rise through halted dilution and radial-selection effects.
mauve_tests: Measure abundance/SFE across the dated quenching front and along the tail, with explicit radius-dependent clocks rather than one galaxy-wide stage.

hi_evidence: The severely truncated disk feeds a roughly 110 x 25 kpc, star-poor H I plume containing about 3.4e8 Msun; this is among the clearest direct gas-removal cases.
multiwavelength_evidence: The 35 kpc ionized VEELR is mostly stripped gas photoionized by the Seyfert nucleus, with shocks in outer/high-velocity regions. X-ray absorption places the H I in front of M86 and favours the main Virgo/M87 atmosphere; CO about 70 kpc down-tail shows inefficient in-situ molecule formation.
event_sequence: A high-pressure encounter removed most outer gas; stripped multiphase material persists far downstream while the active nucleus illuminates, shocks or drives physically distinct ionized components.
timing: The 2009 model is about 150 Myr after peak; updated tailored work gives about 240 Myr after peak, while outer-disk SFHs give 190+/-30 Myr since quenching. These are different clocks, and the tailored peak has no formal statistical error.
contradictions: MAUVE/Yoon near-peak grouping is morphological, while tailored work is post-peak. Later X-ray geometry weakens the earlier tentative M86-halo origin, though local structure can contribute. No single model fits every disk/tail observable; AGN emission must not be counted as stripped-gas star formation.
history_confidence: very high for stripping; high-moderate for exact ICM/orbit
gfmr_implication: Gas loss is extreme, but line ratios are AGN contaminated; SFR-FMR work needs strict HII selection. Tail depletion times of about 1.6e10 to >1.4e12 yr show that gas presence does not imply efficient star formation.
mauve_tests: Separate AGN cone, shocks, extraplanar tail and disk HII emission spectroscopically; use metallicity/velocity continuity to identify stripped parcels.

hi_evidence: A compressed southeastern edge, sharp H I truncation and northwestern extraplanar tail show an ICM wind acting now.
multiwavelength_evidence: Dust filaments reveal ablation and dense-cloud decoupling; ALMA detects compressed and extraplanar molecular gas. Radio polarization/deficit patterns independently locate the windward edge.
event_sequence: Diffuse outer gas was stripped first; denser clouds partially decoupled and are now ablated, while even molecular gas is compressed/displaced.
timing: Outer-disk stellar work gives less than about 200 Myr since local quenching; no single tailored time to peak is as secure as for NGC4330/4501/4522.
contradictions: The current wind is certain, but individual extraplanar dense clouds may be transiently bound or fall back; molecular removal is not uniform.
gfmr_implication: This is a direct demonstration that environment can alter both gas mass and local SFE. Dense surviving clouds and stripped diffuse gas should occupy different resolved gFMR pathways.
mauve_tests: Pair cloud-scale CO, extinction and metallicity with leading/trailing MUSE maps; identify bound versus escaping components kinematically.

primary_mechanism: intermediate-ratio merger remnant plus ongoing ram pressure
hi_evidence: A roughly 110 kpc one-sided H I tail and strongly disturbed central gas coexist with a shell/banana-shaped stellar body.
multiwavelength_evidence: Low V/sigma, possible gas counter-rotation and non-circular CO establish a recent roughly 1:4-1:10 merger. VESTIGE finds outside-in Halpha truncation and an RPS tail, while the opposite 10 kpc NW ionized feature is a shock-excited starburst outflow supported by radio polarization.
event_sequence: A gravitational encounter transformed the stellar disk and concentrated gas; ongoing near-face-on ram pressure removed low-density material, while the central burst powered a distinct outflow.
timing: West/east outer-disk quenching times are 281+/-27 and 251+/-14 Myr; a simple central SFH event is 179+/-68 Myr. The merger is inferred within roughly 500 Myr, not dynamically dated.
contradictions: Yoon II and Köppen active classify the gas morphology but omit the prior merger. The southern stripping tail and NW outflow are physically different; treating all extraplanar gas as one mechanism is wrong.
history_confidence: high for compound history; moderate for detailed ordering
gfmr_implication: Merger-driven inflow/mixing and selective outer removal can be simultaneous; shock/outflow spaxels and non-HII excitation must be excluded before interpreting metallicity residuals.
mauve_tests: Reconstruct stellar populations and metallicity along shells, central inflow and both tails; use gas-star misalignment to time gravity separately from stripping.

hi_evidence: A compressed southwest/southeast H I edge and extended opposite side provide a textbook early-stage wind geometry.
multiwavelength_evidence: Polarized radio ridge and MAUVE ionized-gas asymmetry support current compression; CO studies show multiphase response rather than simple atomic-only loss.
event_sequence: The galaxy is approaching maximum pressure; the leading side is compressed while diffuse gas is displaced to the trailing side, before severe symmetric truncation.
timing: Tailored models place it roughly 200-300 Myr before peak (Vollmer 2009 adopts -250 Myr). Model variants span about 190-320 Myr and depend on pressure profile/orientation.
contradictions: Projected phase space cannot by itself fix the clock; the tailored multi-tracer fit is stronger but still model-dependent. Compression need not imply globally enhanced star formation.
gfmr_implication: This is the clean pre-peak comparator: pressure can redistribute gas and DIG before major gas depletion, potentially altering local SFE/SFR while total gas remains substantial.
mauve_tests: Test leading-versus-trailing metallicity, DIG fraction and CO excitation against the model wind vector; compare with NGC4522 near peak.

hi_evidence: The H I disk is truncated to roughly 0.35 optical radii with abundant extraplanar gas while the stellar disk is undisturbed.
multiwavelength_evidence: HST dust, CO, radio and MUSE all show direct multiphase stripping. New high-resolution radio spectra indicate shock re-acceleration and mixing; extraplanar thermal emission is not solely star formation.
event_sequence: A strong ICM encounter compressed the leading edge, removed diffuse and some molecular gas, and left dense clouds temporarily decoupled in the extraplanar flow.
timing: Tailored modelling gives about 50 Myr after pressure maximum; outer-disk stellar quenching is about 100+/-50 Myr. The pressure excess requires local ICM substructure or relative ICM motion.
contradictions: The adopted near-peak label covers an object that best-fit models place just after peak. Static smooth-ICM models underpredict the required pressure, so orbit-only interpretations are inadequate.
gfmr_implication: Because shocks/mixing add ionized emission and CO-bearing clouds survive, both Halpha SFR and gas mass require phase-aware measurement. The galaxy is a benchmark for non-equilibrium gFMR tracks.
mauve_tests: Separate HII, shock/mixing and DIG components; measure cloud-by-cloud metallicity, CO, and escape/fallback kinematics across the wind interface.

primary_mechanism: tidal interaction plus weak ram pressure
hi_evidence: A long southeastern H I tail and northwestern compressed edge cannot be reproduced simultaneously by a single simple perturbation.
multiwavelength_evidence: Models and polarized radio data favour a close tidal encounter with NGC4639 about 500 Myr ago plus weak ongoing pressure; resolved CO/SF work adds feedback and gas-compression constraints.
event_sequence: Tides pulled gas outward and generated asymmetric stellar/gas structure; weak ram pressure then acted efficiently on the loosened gas and continues to shape the outer arm.
timing: The preferred model places the NGC4639 encounter about 500 Myr ago; ongoing pressure is weak. This is a tidal clock, not time from Virgo pressure peak.
contradictions: Köppen lists the galaxy as non-deficient despite Yoon II morphology; this is expected because strong asymmetry can occur without large integrated deficiency in a mixed tide+RPS event.
gfmr_implication: Tides first change gas geometry, then weak pressure removes exposed gas; local SFE/metallicity effects can precede a large global H I deficit.
mauve_tests: Map abundance and SFE separately in the tidal inner arm, pressure-dominated outer arm and tail; compare to the published wind/encounter geometry.

hi_evidence: A coherent 38-50 kpc, roughly 1.1e9 Msun H I bridge/debris complex connects NGC4694 with the tidal-dwarf candidate VCC2062; its structure, high column density and stellar bridge favour gravity over a clean wind tail.
multiwavelength_evidence: CO, young stars and 12+log(O/H) about 8.6-8.7 in VCC2062 prove recycled, pre-enriched tidal material. Molecular depletion times are roughly 1-2e10 yr and can reach 6e10 yr locally.
event_sequence: A slow unequal-mass gas-rich merger produced the bridge and tidal dwarf; ram pressure may reshape the debris but is not the primary explanation.
timing: The completed single-nucleus merger is inferred to be several hundred Myr old. CIGALE burst ages are 376+/-99 Myr globally and 313+/-86 Myr in the CO region; neither is a pressure-peak clock.
contradictions: Yoon II is contaminated by counting a tidal bridge as a one-sided stripping feature, and Yoon notes the within-disk morphology resembles class III. Köppen's analytical past-strip label is weaker than the dedicated tidal evidence.
history_confidence: very high for tidal history; low for ICM history
gfmr_implication: VCC2062 is pre-enriched recycled gas, not pristine inflow or ordinary dwarf chemistry. Merger mixing/inflow may affect NGC4694, but its resolved abundance history remains unmeasured.
mauve_tests: Use MUSE metallicity/kinematic continuity from disk to bridge and combine with CO to distinguish recycled accretion from any stripped component.

primary_mechanism: past ram pressure plus gravitational disturbance
hi_evidence: H I is confined to the inner few kiloparsecs and strongly deficient, while the outer stellar body is much less truncated.
multiwavelength_evidence: Non-circular gas and central star formation indicate a gravitational perturbation. MAUVE-MUSE now directly resolves a bipolar ionized outflow with mass loading about 1.66 from the remaining central gas.
event_sequence: A past encounter/stripping episode removed the outer gas and concentrated what survived; approximately 0.4 Gyr later, residual central star formation is driving a wind that may accelerate final quenching.
timing: Outer-disk stellar quenching is about 425+/-75 Myr. The outflow depletion argument is current and uncertain in electron density/geometry; much outflowing gas may remain bound.
contradictions: RPS alone does not explain all non-circular/stellar features. Feedback is a late-stage mechanism, not evidence that the original stripping was feedback-driven.
history_confidence: high for past processing and current outflow; moderate for mechanism ordering
gfmr_implication: This is a two-step path: environmental gas loss changes gas fraction, then feedback changes SFR and observable ionized gas. It can depart from equilibrium gFMR expectations in more than one direction.
mauve_tests: Measure outflow metallicity and escape fraction, central CO depletion, and stellar-age asymmetry to separate the prior gravitational and hydrodynamic events.

primary_mechanism: long-term gas depletion plus satellite accretion
hi_evidence: The H I disk is fairly regular but low surface density and deficient, without a clear current stripping edge.
multiwavelength_evidence: Deep optical imaging to about 29 mag arcsec^-2 reveals multiple streams, loops and disrupting dwarfs, directly proving ongoing gravitational bombardment; no extended group X-ray halo is detected.
event_sequence: Slow/older gas depletion and repeated minor accretion coexist; the streams need not have caused the H I deficiency, and an ICM or viscous-stripping history remains plausible.
timing: No unique pressure clock. Stream survival is probably shorter than about 1 Gyr. A core passage at least roughly 1 Gyr ago is a travel-time scenario, not a fitted orbit.
contradictions: Yoon IV and Köppen past imply evolved gas processing, but Paudel establishes satellite interactions and leaves the stripping epoch ambiguous. Nearby NGC4222 has regular H I, so a simple bound-group preprocessing narrative is not demonstrated.
history_confidence: high for minor accretion; low for gas-loss epoch
gfmr_implication: Tidal accretion can add stars/gas while slow stripping removes diffuse H I, making global gas and metallicity histories non-monotonic; the streams alone do not demonstrate metal-poor inflow.
mauve_tests: Use MUSE stellar populations/kinematics at stream interfaces and compare outer-disk gas metallicity to test whether accreted material reached the disk.

hi_evidence: The galaxy is extremely H I deficient with gas confined centrally; absorption and non-circular motions are prominent.
multiwavelength_evidence: A misaligned/disturbed stellar-gas configuration and strong bar/central activity point to gravitational/internal redistribution in addition to environmental removal.
event_sequence: Outer atomic gas was removed in an earlier passage; surviving gas settled or was driven into the centre by non-axisymmetric dynamics.
timing: No direct stellar clock in the core set; analytical work calls it a past stripper/possible backsplash case.
contradictions: The gas deficit supports past removal, but the central kinematics cannot be assigned to RPS. Phase-space backsplash is probabilistic.
gfmr_implication: Loss of metal-poor outskirts and central aperture weighting can elevate measured metallicity without requiring closed-box enrichment; bar-driven SFE is a separate variable.
mauve_tests: Measure age/metallicity at the truncation boundary and model bar versus external gas kinematics; avoid AGN/DIG spaxels.

hi_evidence: H I is mildly asymmetric, low surface brightness and deficient but lacks an active one-sided wind morphology.
multiwavelength_evidence: The disk is anemic; CO and radio surveys provide measurements without a dedicated event reconstruction.
event_sequence: A slow process or relaxed remnant of an older stripping event reduced diffuse gas and star formation without leaving a strong current tail.
timing: No direct clock.
contradictions: Yoon IV supports slow processes; Köppen labels past stripping. Current observations do not discriminate starvation, evaporation, or relaxed RPS.
history_confidence: moderate for processed status; low for mechanism
gfmr_implication: A slow fall in gas supply can move the system closer to equilibrium than impulsive stripping; radial aperture loss can still mimic metallicity enhancement.
mauve_tests: Use stellar ages and outer-disk abundance gradients to distinguish prolonged starvation from an abrupt old truncation.

hi_evidence: The H I disk is deficient and mildly truncated but strikingly symmetric.
multiwavelength_evidence: The galaxy is anemic. Although projected near M85, VIVA reports no decisive tidal signature linking the two.
event_sequence: Gas supply/removal acted gently or long enough ago for the disk to relax; no active stripping evidence remains.
timing: No published event clock and no Köppen entry.
contradictions: Yoon IV supplies only a morphology class. Association with M85 is contextual, not causal evidence.
gfmr_implication: This is a useful test of slow gas exhaustion: lower gas and SFR may remain coupled, unlike impulsive stripping, but aperture/radial effects must be controlled.
mauve_tests: Derive spatially resolved SFHs and gas-star misalignment; search for subtle M85-facing age or metallicity asymmetry.

hi_evidence: The H I disk is severely and symmetrically truncated while the stellar disk is regular, with little evidence for current pressure.
multiwavelength_evidence: Outer-disk stellar populations are quenched; broad CO/survey data do not identify a competing gravitational event.
event_sequence: An earlier ICM passage removed outer gas; the remaining inner disk has since relaxed.
timing: Outer-disk quenching is about 450+/-150 Myr.
contradictions: Yoon III and Köppen past agree. The clock dates cessation of local star formation, not necessarily exact pressure maximum.
gfmr_implication: A post-stripping system should show low gas fraction and radially censored star formation; metallicity offsets can arise from outside-in removal and halted dilution.
mauve_tests: Measure metallicity/ages immediately inside and outside the old truncation radius and search for fallback gas.

hi_evidence: The H I disk is extremely small relative to the stars; extraplanar/absorption features suggest residual displacement or fallback.
multiwavelength_evidence: The stellar disk is comparatively undisturbed. CO is centrally concentrated and historical observations show asymmetry; MAUVE ionized-gas data sample a strongly processed disk.
event_sequence: A strong event removed outer gas; surviving/fallback material and central dynamics now dominate the inner disk.
timing: Outer-disk quenching is about 500+/-150 Myr (individual indicators vary). No current pressure maximum is inferred.
contradictions: The regular stellar disk favours hydrodynamic removal, while central non-axisymmetry may be internal. Negative line-of-sight velocity makes phase-space placement projection sensitive.
gfmr_implication: Strong radial truncation changes which metallicities enter integrated measurements; central gas retention can preserve SFR at very low H I mass.
mauve_tests: Search for kinematically distinct fallback gas and compare central molecular SFE to the quenched outer-disk age gradient.

hi_evidence: H I is moderately truncated and low surface density but symmetric, with no current tail or compressed edge.
multiwavelength_evidence: Anemic star formation coexists with a bar and low-luminosity AGN; these internal processes complicate ionized-gas interpretation.
event_sequence: Diffuse gas was slowly removed/starved or stripped long ago; the present gas disk is relaxed.
timing: No direct quenching or pressure clock.
contradictions: Yoon IV and Köppen past agree on an evolved state but not on mechanism. AGN emission is not evidence of environment.
gfmr_implication: Slow depletion and AGN/DIG contamination make Halpha-based SFR especially vulnerable; gas-based relations may better record the environmental deficit.
mauve_tests: Use HII-only masks, stellar ages and outer CO/H I limits to distinguish starvation from old impulsive stripping.

hi_evidence: The H I disk is severely, nearly symmetrically truncated while the stellar disk remains regular.
multiwavelength_evidence: Outer-disk stars record cessation of star formation; no dedicated gravitational alternative is established.
event_sequence: A strong ICM event removed outer gas, after which the remaining disk relaxed.
timing: Outer-disk quenching is about 500+/-100 Myr.
contradictions: Yoon III and Köppen past agree; the stellar clock is local and does not uniquely reconstruct the orbit.
gfmr_implication: The system anchors a clean post-stripping path in which low gas fraction and radial censorship precede continued central evolution.
mauve_tests: Measure the abundance step/gradient across the truncation radius and compare central molecular SFE to other post-peak disks.

hi_evidence: The H I disk is small and asymmetric/warped but lacks a strong current wind signature.
multiwavelength_evidence: Radio and MAUVE ionized-gas surveys reveal a processed disk but no dedicated orbital model; internal structure remains plausible.
event_sequence: An earlier mild-to-moderate removal episode and/or minor accretion disturbed gas; the present event status is relaxed.
timing: No published clock; Köppen does not include the galaxy.
contradictions: Yoon III implies severe/past morphology, but VIVA describes a less decisive active signature. Mechanism confidence is limited.
gfmr_implication: Gas warps/accretion can change metallicity and kinematics independently of stripping, so a post label alone cannot set the expected FMR residual.
mauve_tests: Test gas-star misalignment and azimuthal metallicity asymmetry; determine whether the warp carries distinct abundance.

hi_evidence: The H I disk is mildly truncated and low surface density; it is an anemic galaxy without a convincing present wind tail.
multiwavelength_evidence: A strong bar dominates gas kinematics. LOFAR supplies environmental radio context but does not yield a unique stripping history.
event_sequence: Gas supply was reduced gradually or in an older event; the surviving disk evolved secularly under the bar.
timing: No robust time. Earlier kinematic work explicitly questioned whether stripping is still active.
contradictions: Yoon IV and Köppen past support an evolved state, while direct evidence cannot choose starvation versus relaxed RPS.
gfmr_implication: Bar-driven SFE and slow gas depletion are degenerate in SFR-based FMR projections; spatial gas mass and stellar ages are needed.
mauve_tests: Model bar streaming before searching for weak wind residuals; compare outer-disk ages to gas truncation.

hi_evidence: The H I disk is only about one third of the stellar extent and is highly deficient; extraplanar material and a newly traced 230 kpc Halpha tail record removed gas.
multiwavelength_evidence: A magnetized/nuclear outflow is distinct from the stripping tail. Spectroscopy along the 230 kpc tail shows a smooth velocity gradient toward the Virgo systemic velocity, directly tracing deceleration of stripped ISM.
event_sequence: A major pressure event removed the outer disk about 0.3 Gyr ago; a central wind developed from surviving gas while stripped clouds mixed with and decelerated in the ICM.
timing: Tailored gas models and outer stellar populations both give about 300 Myr since peak/quenching (stellar uncertainty about 50 Myr). The far Halpha tail implies cloud survival at least about 0.5 Gyr under model assumptions.
contradictions: The nuclear outflow contains far less mass than the stripped component and must not be used to explain the global deficiency. The 230 kpc tail strengthens RPS but cloud survival/mixing physics remain uncertain.
gfmr_implication: This galaxy combines genuine gas removal, long-lived ionized tail emission and a central wind; Halpha outside the disk is not in-situ SFR, while gas fraction strongly departs from equilibrium expectations.
mauve_tests: Use tail metallicity/line ratios and MUSE disk SFHs to connect the 300 Myr event to present central SFE; exclude wind/tail emission from disk FMR fits.

hi_evidence: The H I disk is moderately and symmetrically truncated, without a clear current tail.
multiwavelength_evidence: A bar and LINER/Seyfert nucleus dominate central molecular and ionized-gas behavior.
event_sequence: Environmental gas loss/starvation acted in the past or slowly; the present disk is relaxed and central secular/AGN processes now dominate.
timing: No environmental clock.
contradictions: Yoon IV and Köppen past agree only at the broad level. AGN/torque studies are not environmental evidence.
gfmr_implication: AGN/DIG and bar inflow contaminate SFR/metallicity diagnostics; gas-based deficits should be interpreted separately from central emission.
mauve_tests: Apply conservative HII masks and compare outer stellar ages to H I/CO truncation, after subtracting bar streaming.

hi_evidence: A severely truncated H I disk sits inside a regular stellar disk with no present tail.
multiwavelength_evidence: Outer-disk stellar populations are quenched; the retained central disk continues limited star formation.
event_sequence: A past ICM event stripped the outer disk, after which the galaxy moved to its current projected location and the gas morphology relaxed.
timing: Outer-disk quenching is about 475+/-100 Myr. Backsplash status is a phase-space/model inference, not directly observed.
contradictions: Yoon III and Köppen past converge. The current large projected radius does not uniquely prove a core passage.
history_confidence: high for past stripping; moderate for backsplash
gfmr_implication: The galaxy is a strong post-event test of how metallicity and SFE evolve for roughly half a Gyr after abrupt outside-in gas loss.
mauve_tests: Derive a resolved age-metallicity profile across the fossil truncation and search for reaccreted/fallback gas.

hi_evidence: H I occupies only a small fraction of the stellar disk and is strongly deficient.
multiwavelength_evidence: The stellar morphology is disturbed, so tides/harassment likely contributed; no dedicated tailored model fixes the balance.
event_sequence: A gravitational perturbation altered the stellar disk and environmental pressure removed most diffuse gas, in uncertain order.
timing: No direct clock; Köppen treats it as a past stripper.
contradictions: Yoon III and Köppen past support an evolved gas state, but a pure-RPS narrative is inconsistent with the disturbed stars.
gfmr_implication: Tidal inflow and gas stripping can offset one another in SFR and metallicity, making an integrated post-peak residual non-unique.
mauve_tests: Use stellar/gas kinematic misalignment and SFHs to order the tidal and stripping events; constrain remaining central CO SFE.

primary_mechanism: past or ongoing ram pressure stripping
hi_evidence: The edge-on H I disk is truncated and deficient.
multiwavelength_evidence: The approximately 600 km/s velocity difference and lack of a clear tidal bridge weaken the idea that NGC4606 is a bound perturber. LOFAR identifies NGC4607 as a new radio-RPS candidate.
event_sequence: ICM interaction likely truncated the disk; apparent pairing with NGC4606 may be mostly projection rather than the cause.
timing: No tailored time.
contradictions: Yoon III/Köppen past imply a relaxed event, whereas current radio asymmetry may indicate residual/renewed pressure. This is a real status tension, not an error.
gfmr_implication: Radio evidence can persist or reveal current pressure after H I truncation; gas mass and SFR clocks may therefore be asynchronous.
mauve_tests: Use MUSE DIG/shock asymmetry and radio spectral aging to decide whether pressure is still active; test the pair hypothesis with stellar velocities.

hi_evidence: The H I disk is mildly and symmetrically truncated with no clear current wind feature.
multiwavelength_evidence: Rich CO/cloud measurements characterize the inner disk but do not supply a dedicated environmental event clock.
event_sequence: A slow process or old weak stripping reduced the outer gas; the present disk is relaxed.
timing: No direct clock.
contradictions: Yoon IV and Köppen past agree broadly but cannot distinguish starvation from old RPS.
gfmr_implication: This is a slow-processing comparison where gas and SFR may evolve together more nearly than in active strippers; resolved cloud physics remains an internal confounder.
mauve_tests: Compare cloud-scale SFE and stellar ages across the H I truncation, using PHANGS/VERTICO resolution matching.

primary_mechanism: ancient external accretion plus uncertain weak cluster stripping
hi_evidence: The H I disk extends to roughly twice the stellar disk and is mostly regular; two short SE tails and NW compression are only tentative weak/incipient RPS indicators, not a classic post-stripping remnant.
multiwavelength_evidence: Orthogonal bulge/disk and a polar stellar+gas nuclear disk directly prove ancient external acquisition. Its stellar population requires star formation to have ended more than 5 Gyr ago, unrelated to any demonstrated present Virgo event.
event_sequence: An ancient accretion event built the decoupled central structure; a separate incipient, weak or past ICM event remains possible but is not reconstructed by a dedicated modern processing study.
timing: No tailored RPS clock. The polar event is older than 5 Gyr; Köppen's past-strip label is analytical and carries at least factor-of-two pressure uncertainty.
contradictions: This is the second reclassification audit: Yoon I/VIVA indicate weak or early processing with projection ambiguity, while Köppen labels it past. MAUVE retains post-peak as a sample code, but confidence in that ICM chronology is low; Corsini supports ancient accretion, not post-peak RPS or proven preprocessing.
history_confidence: high for ancient accretion; low for adopted post-peak ICM status
gfmr_implication: The ancient polar component may cause central chemical/kinematic decoupling but is not evidence for current dilution. Very low SFR and uncertain gas processing make either FMR projection non-unique.
mauve_tests: Date separate stellar components, map metallicity/kinematics of the extended H I-linked disk, and test M49-substructure membership with distances rather than projected phase space alone.
